meta.title: Md. Hossain | IT Infrastructure Specialist, Dhaka, Bangladesh
meta.description: Md. Hossain is a Dhaka-based IT professional and founder of Fixible IT with 8+ years in enterprise IT: Microsoft 365, Active Directory, MikroTik networks, site-to-site VPN and IP CCTV.
hero.lead: I design and run the IT that growing businesses depend on: networks that connect every office, Microsoft 365 and Active Directory that simply work, and surveillance systems that keep recording. Eight years in Bangladeshi manufacturing and group companies, supporting 150+ people across four offices.
scene.aria: Rotating 3D illustration of a multi-site business network: a cloud and internet layer connected to a head office and two branch offices by site-to-site VPN tunnels. Each office has a router or firewall, switch, Wi-Fi access point, workstations, IP cameras and an NVR.
scene.note: Illustrative topology for explanation only. It does not represent any employer’s network. Hover or tap a device to see its role.
about.title: Keeping people and systems connected
about.p1: My IT career began in 2018 on the support desk of a Bangladeshi manufacturer, keeping 250+ people productive on the factory floor and in the office. Since 2020 I have been Senior IT Officer at MKR Group, responsible for users, networks and security systems across four regional offices.
about.p2: I care about the quiet kind of IT: networks that stay up, accounts that are created and removed correctly, cameras that keep recording, and documentation that lets someone else take over tomorrow.
about.p3: I founded Fixible IT to bring the same standards to small businesses and homes in Bangladesh, with IT services and an online store for technology products. In my own time I build small Windows tools in Python.
about.quote: Practical expertise, sensible automation and customer-focused service, applied to real problems.

cloud: Microsoft 365 and other online services: email, identity and files, reached over the internet.
isp: The public network that links every office. Link health and ISP escalation live here.
fw: Filters traffic, performs NAT and terminates the site-to-site VPN tunnels.
rt: MikroTik-class edge router: internet access, routing and the VPN tunnel back to head office.
sw: Connects wired devices and keeps traffic separated into VLANs.
srv: On-premises services such as file shares, directory or management tools.
ap: Wireless coverage. Channel planning and authentication decide how reliable it feels.
pc: Where most support work ends: set-up, access, updates and troubleshooting.
cam: Powered over Ethernet (PoE), streaming video to the NVR on its own VLAN.
nvr: Network video recorder: records the cameras and keeps footage for the retention period.

rk.title: Inside a business server rack
rk.sub: Scroll to walk through the equipment that keeps an office running, from the internet connection down to the backup power.
rk.aria: 3D illustration of a server rack containing an edge firewall, patch panel, core switch, two servers, a network video recorder and a UPS. As you scroll, each unit is highlighted, then the rack dissolves into binary digits.
rk.u1.d: Connects the office to the internet, filters traffic and builds the encrypted VPN tunnels to other branches.
rk.u2.d: Every cable from desks, cameras and access points ends here, labelled, so any port can be traced in seconds.
rk.u3.d: Moves traffic between every wired device and keeps staff, guests and cameras apart in separate VLANs.
rk.u4.d: File shares, directory services and management tools that need to stay inside the building.
rk.u5.d: Records every IP camera on its own network and keeps footage for the agreed retention period.
rk.u6.d: Keeps everything running through short power cuts and shuts systems down safely during long ones.
rk.end.t: Underneath it all: ones and zeros
rk.end.d: Every email, file and video frame that passes through the rack is binary data in the end. Keep scrolling and watch it come apart.
